newsitem.title: JAPAN: Strong quake rocks southern Japan, no casualties.
newsitem.headline: Strong quake rocks southern Japan, no casualties.

text.p: A strong earthquake measuring 7.0 on the Richter scale jolted Japan's southernmost main island of Kyushu late on Saturday, but there were no immediate reports of casualties.

The tremor rocked the island at 11.44 p.m. (1444 GMT) and registered "lower 5" on the 7-point Japanese intensity scale in the cities of Miyazaki and Kanoya in southern Kyushu, the Meteorological Agency said.

The quake also recorded a four on the Japanese scale in Kurume, Kumamoto, Oita and other Kyushu cities. It was felt over most of Kyushu and western parts of the main island of Honshu, the agency said.

The agency issued "tsunami" or tidal wave warnings for the Inland Sea coastline of Yamaguchi, Wakayama and Hyogo prefectures, the Sea of Japan coastline of Yamaguchi Prefecture, the Pacific coastline of Shikoku Island, the western coast of Kyushu, and Okinawa.
The focus of the earthquake was some 40 kilometres (25 miles) under the seabed in the Pacific Ocean, some 50 km (31 miles) east-southeast of Miyazaki city.
The quake was the strongest of a series of quakes that had occurred throughout the day, beginning around noon, the agency said.
Aftershocks from the latest quake are continuing, it said.
